text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: PD#84231 — GPU memory pressure detected on pool `gpu-pool-7` (region-us-west1). Symptom: repeated CUDA allocation failures and elevated eviction rates. Auto-suppression: false.

pagerduty: Incident PD#84231 triggered by rule `gpu.kvcache.alloc_failures >= 10m` — paging primary oncall.

Olivia: acked. I'm grabbing this — oncall Olivia here. first check: customer impact?

Maria: seeing increased 5xx errors for two customers hitting long-context workloads. Telemetry shows mean latency spikes from 120ms -> 1.2s for the pool in last 7m.

Ken: stack traces show `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY` and frequent `cudaMallocRetry` logs. Also kvcache eviction rate has spiked 5x.

Ajay: looks like fragmentation, not total memory. free memory fluctuates a lot, allocations fail at mid-level sizes. suspect kvcache prefetch + long sequence batches.

Olivia: thanks — steps: 1) reduce kvcache prefetch on pool 7 2) drain large-batch model routes 3) scale up capacity (if possible) 4) escalate to L2 if not stabilizing in 10m.

Maria: doing quick impact note to customers: "We're investigating intermittent GPU memory failures causing higher latencies; routing fallbacks enabled where possible."

Ken: running exploit probe to see which model instance is causing largest fragmentation. paste logs snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T14:03:12Z] model=redwood-rlhf-v2 instance=gpud-7-3 cuda: alloc(2.1GiB) -> ERROR: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
[2026-03-15T14:03:13Z] kvcache evict rate=832/s -> avg=87/s baseline
[2026-03-15T14:03:14Z] backend: allocation latency jitter=320ms -> 1.8s
```

ops-bot: Suggested action: `drain-host gpud-7-3`, `set-route-weight large-batch 0.0 --pool gpu-pool-7`, `kvcache-prefetch disable --pool gpu-pool-7 --scope model:redwood-rlhf-v2`.

Olivia: executing quick mitigations now. Ken, can you confirm which instances to drain? Ajay, can you prepare a canary fallback to CPU for the affected models?

Ajay: prepping cpu-fallback image. ETA ~6m. I'll bump concurrency to avoid overload.

Ken: target instances: gpud-7-3, gpud-7-5 are hottest. I'll issue drains for those two.

Olivia: running commands:
```
# mark instances unhealthy to stop new allocations
infra@cli$ rtdb set-instance-attr gpud-7-3 unhealthy --reason "oom-frag-emergency"
infra@cli$ rtdb set-instance-attr gpud-7-5 unhealthy --reason "oom-frag-emergency"
# reduce route weight for large batches
infra@cli$ redwood route update --route large-batch --pool gpu-pool-7 --weight 0.0
# disable kvcache prefetch for pool
infra@cli$ redwood kvcache update --pool gpu-pool-7 --prefetch off
```

sre-bot: Auto-scaler triggered +1 instance in pool `gpu-pool-7` (gpud-7-9) — warmup in progress.

Maria: telemetry after mitigations: eviction rate down to 210/s, allocation failure rate reduced by ~60% in the last 3m. Latency still elevated for some requests due to retries.

Olivia: good. Maria — please prepare short customer msg for the two affected tenants (internal ticket ids: C-1982, C-1988). Include: what happened, mitigation, ETA for full recovery.

Maria: drafting. Also flagging for follow-up: need long-term fix for kvcache fragmentation.

Ken: L2 advise: try `cudaMallocAsync` pool tuning, and consider enabling slab allocator temporarily. Jia from infra, can you take L2?

Jia: taking L2. On the way in. Quick questions: can we afford preemptive evictions on noncritical models? Any cost constraints?

Olivia: prioritize customer-facing tenants. Evict noncritical caches aggressively. Cost ok for now.

Jia: running targeted eviction script:
```
infra@ops$ python scripts/evict_kvcache.py --pool gpu-pool-7 --exclude-tenants C-1982,C-1988 --target-percent 40
# TTL-based eviction for older prefixes
```

ops-bot: Action logged: `evict_kvcache` by Jia, job id evict-8032.

Ken: after targeted eviction, allocation failures dropped to near-zero and mean latency trending to normal. Looks like fragmentation coupled with aggressive prefetch on a few tenants triggered the cascade.

pagerduty: PD#84231 acknowledged by Olivia at 14:04 UTC; reassigned to L2 Jia at 14:08 UTC.

Maria: customer update ready: "We've mitigated GPU memory fragmentation causing intermittent allocation failures. We've drained affected instances and disabled aggressive kvcache prefetch. A new instance was added to the pool. We're continuing to monitor and will follow up with a post-incident summary." Shall I send?

Olivia: send and mark incident as monitoring.

Maria: sent to contacts for C-1982/C-1988. Both acknowledged and reported degraded but improving behavior.

Jia: follow-up runbook items: 1) add a circuit-breaker for kvcache prefetch per-tenant 2) expose fragmentation alert metric 3) explore slab allocator or tuned cudaMallocAsync flags 4) schedule postmortem.

Ajay: also recommend adding model-level soft-limits for batch size on gpu pools and smarter fallback routing for long-sequence jobs.

Olivia: agreed. I'm putting a short action list in the incident ticket and handing back to oncall rotation. Any objections to closing PD and moving to postmortem?

Ken: +1. Root cause hypothesis: long-sequence workloads with aggressive kvcache prefetch produced fragmented allocations causing mid-size alloc failures and retry storms. Immediate mitigations successful.

sre-bot: PD#84231 auto-resolve check: allocations stable for 12m, eviction rate normal.

pagerduty: PD#84231 resolved at 14:21 UTC by Olivia.

Olivia: closing thread here. Postmortem owners: Jia (infra), Ken (runtime), Ajay (models), Maria (customer comms). I'll add timelines and attach logs. Great coordination, thanks all. :heart: 

Ken: adding follow-ups to backlog: `RUNTIME-1214` (slab allocator experiment), `KVC-87` (prefetch circuit breaker), `OBS-452` (fragmentation metric).

Maria: will sync with support to ensure customers get final post-incident summary tomorrow.

incident-bot: Incident PD#84231 -> status: resolved; duration: 18m; responders: Olivia, Jia, Ken, Maria, Ajay.

Olivia: linking to incident ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-84231 and handoff complete.
